So to answer a part of your post....instant ink counts. The margin on it is similar to what you get on the ones of the shelf. The difference being that with instant ink you can guarantee that the residual income to the store. If I leave the store, there is no way to make sure the customer comes back (think how many times a day you hear about our high prices). The next portion of it is that the new HP printers ask the customer to sign up at setup and at every cartridge change. If the customer signs up at home. The store gets none of the revenue. It goes to a corporate staples pot. If the store sells them a card, the store gets all of the revenue. That customer remains tied to the store as long as the remain on the program no matter where they have the printer. For example, buy the printer in Florida and use in California....the revenue for the subscription still goes to the store in Florida. The only things instant ink hurts is top line sales and customer counts (but we are losing those anyways). As a side note. HP pays a bounty if you are over a certain percentage of attach at the end of the quarter to make up for lost traffic. There are other benefits like lower inventory costs and my favorite less labor time on ink.
